title: Measurement of gastrointestinal and colonic transit in mice
protocol: Induce and maintain anesthesia using isoflurane in oxygen.
Tape the mouse's feet to the operating table with its head away from the operator.
Adjust direct halogen illumination to an appropriate intensity for the operation.
Shave the abdomen using hair clippers and sterilize the skin with Kodan.
Make a 2 cm mid-line skin incision distally from the xiphisternum.
Enter the peritoneal cavity via an incision along the linea alba made using a straight forceps and sterile small scissor.
Keep the abdomen open with two retractors and place sterile moist cotton pads around the incision.
Carefully eventrate the small intestine with two saline-moistened cotton buds onto the sterile cotton pads.
Carefully unfold the small bowel loops on the cotton pads and run it once with moderate compression from oral to aboral direction using two moist cotton buds.
Carefully replace the intestine back into the abdomen with moist cotton buds.
Complete surgical closure of the peritoneal cavity by two continuous sutures using the needle holder, straight forceps, and suture material.
Terminate anesthesia and allow the animal to recover from the surgery under a heating lamp.
Inspect the animal and wound closure for signs of infection or other complications after 22.5 hours.
Replace the animals under anesthesia using isoflurane in oxygen.
Hyperextend the animal's head.
Use a forceps to carefully pull out the tongue.
Feed forward an arterial catheter connected to a 1ml syringe into the mouth.
Push the catheter forward into the stomach.
Check patency of the colon by inserting a polished metal rod 3cm into the colon.
Pull out the rod and insert a 2mm glass ball transanally with a blunt surgical forceps.
Carefully feed the glass ball forward for 3cm into the colon with a polished metal rod.
Put the animal in a box allowing observation and measurement of the colonic transit time as the time from insertion until excretion of the glass ball.
Replace the animals under deep anesthesia using isoflurane.
Maintain anesthesia if additional analyses require the animal to remain alive.
Kill the animal by cervical dislocation if only GIT measurement is needed.
Reopen the abdomen using small scissors and straight forceps.
Remove the complete GI tract by subdiaphragmal transection of the esophagus and colon.
Place the GI tract in chilled KHB and inspect for integrity and hematomas.
Transect attaching mesentery arcades to unfold the organ completely.
Place the intestine onto a foil-covered polystyrene pad without stretching.
Measure the full length of the small bowel and colon separately.
Divide the small bowel into 10 equally-sized segments.
Mark the segments by pinning them onto the polystyrene pad with needles.
Proceed in the same manner with the colon but divide it into 3 segments.
Transect the intestine at the marked positions.
Flush the lumen of each intestinal segment twice with 1 ml of KHB.
Store flushed intestinal segments in cold KHB buffer for further analysis.
Transect the stomach and cecum longitudinally.
Place transected stomach and cecum completely into a 2 ml tube with 1 ml KHB.
Vortex all tubes vigorously for at least 10 seconds.
Spin down tubes at 1500xg for 5 minutes.
Transfer supernatants into new 2 ml tubes.
Recentrifuge the supernatants at 11,000xg for 5 minutes.
Pipette 200 µl duplicates of the supernatant into a black 96-well plate.
Measure fluorescence with an excitation/emission wavelength of 494/521 nm.
Subtract blank values (KHB) from measured fluorescence values.
